# cypher-brain

> Encrypt a growing second-brain snapshot (gbrain, Claude Code memory, an Obsidian
> vault, a ChatGPT export) client-side with age (X25519 + ChaCha20-Poly1305), then
> push the ciphertext to a pluggable storage backend — permanently on Arweave
> (recommended), or on TON Storage (self-hosted `ton`, or provider-paid
> `ton-provider`). Storage backends only ever see ciphertext. Recovery needs
> just the identity file and a locator — no wallet, no npm package, to pull the
> bytes back.

## Quickstart

```sh
npx cypher-brain init   # interactive wizard: keygen -> backup key -> first snapshot+push -> recovery kit
```

`init` requires stdin to be a TTY and refuses to run non-interactively (e.g. an AI
agent's shell). For non-interactive/scripted setup, drive the individual commands
it wraps (keygen, snapshot, push) by hand instead — see README.md's "Manual flow"
(which also covers `schedule install` for ongoing unattended runs).

## Driving this CLI as an agent (#347)

stderr is load-bearing, not decoration. If you run cypher-brain on a human's behalf:

- Warnings are ⚠-prefixed on stderr, and every run that produced any ends with a block
  headed `⚠  run summary — N warning(s) a human should see` — **relay that block to
  your human verbatim**. It repeats every warning from the run (a snapshot encrypted to
  a single unrecoverable key, a spend shortfall, a loose-permissioned secret file):
  these exist precisely to reach a person, and a log file they never read does not count.
- The MCP tools return the same content structurally: results carry a `warnings` array
  when the call recorded any (alongside `log`). Surface those to your human too.
- stdout is machine-readable data (a push prints ONLY the locator; `--json` prints one
  JSON document). Parse stdout; relay stderr's summary. The exit code is the sole
  authority on success.

## Key concepts

- **identity** (private key) — the only thing that can decrypt. Lives off the
  always-on machine; lose it and the snapshots are unrecoverable. `keygen --pq`
  generates a post-quantum HYBRID identity (ML-KEM-768 + X25519) instead of
  plain X25519 — see README.md's Threat model.
- **recipient** (public key) — all the snapshotting machine needs. Safe to keep
  on the box that runs gbrain.
- **backend** — pluggable `push`/`pull` storage behind one interface: `file`
  (local, dev/CI), `turbo` (recommended — Arweave via a bundler, ETH/USDC),
  `arweave` (raw L1, small artifacts only), `rclone` (delegates to the `rclone`
  binary and its own configured remote — 70+ providers; cypher-brain's own
  part is free like `file`, the remote's real transfer/storage cost is
  whatever your own cloud contract charges), `ton` (TON Storage seeded from
  your OWN always-on box over SSH; pull is a credential-less P2P download by
  bag id, with a loud fallback to the seeder — free per upload, but NOT
  permanent: retrievable only while a reachable seeder retains the bag),
  `ton-provider` (TON Storage paid to a live third-party provider from
  mytonprovider.org instead of a seeder box you run yourself — signed via a
  Tonkeeper deeplink by default, or auto-signed with a local TON wallet;
  also NOT permanent — depends on the chosen provider staying up).
  `publish-latest` is a separate, opt-in command that points a .ton DNS domain's
  storage record at the latest ton bag (never run automatically) — the CLI
  never signs; it only prints a Tonkeeper deeplink for the operator to approve.
- **recovery kit** — the printable artifact `init` produces: the backup identity
  (raw, not passphrase-wrapped — keep the kit itself physically secure), the
  latest locator, and restore steps. Kit-only recovery on a fresh machine needs
  both the backup key (`init` defaults to generating one, but it can be
  declined) and a portable backend (`turbo`/`arweave`/`ton`/`ton-provider` —
  `file` locators are machine-local). After later pushes, the CLI-only
  `cypher-brain recovery-kit` regenerates it against the current locator (no
  MCP tool on purpose: the kit can embed private key blocks, which must never
  enter agent context).
- **signing keypair** (optional, `keygen --sign`) — age gives confidentiality +
  tamper detection but not *authenticity* (a recipient's public key is not a
  secret, so anyone holding it can forge decryptable ciphertext). A separate
  minisign-compatible Ed25519 signing key addresses the forged-ciphertext half:
  `snapshot` writes a detached `*.minisig` alongside the ciphertext whenever a
  signing identity is present, and `restore`/`verify` check it BEFORE
  decrypting — see README.md's Threat model. By default this is additive: an
  unsigned artifact (no signing key configured, or `snapshot --no-sign`)
  restores exactly as before, which also means an attacker can strip a
  `*.minisig` sidecar instead of forging one and it looks like a legitimate
  unsigned backup. Pass `--require-signature` to `restore`/`verify` to close
  that half too, once every artifact you expect to check is actually signed.

## Everyday commands

```sh
cypher-brain --version                                          # the installed version, bare, on stdout
cypher-brain <command> --help                                   # just that command's flags (--help alone = everything)
cypher-brain keygen                                             # one-time identity + recipient
cypher-brain wallet create                                      # one-time JWK/TON wallet setup for paid backends
cypher-brain doctor                                             # environment, keys, dependencies health check
cypher-brain snapshot --dir <path> --recipient <file> --out <f.age>
cypher-brain verify --in <f.age>                                # real ciphertext? wrong key rejected?
cypher-brain push --in <f.age> --backend turbo --yes             # pays a one-time bundler fee
cypher-brain pull --locator <id> --backend turbo --out <f.age>   # plain gateway fetch, no wallet
cypher-brain restore --in <f.age> --out-dir <dir>
cypher-brain ledger                                             # spend history and storage cost ledger
cypher-brain audit                                              # tamper detection and integrity verification
cypher-brain schedule install --backend turbo --dir <path> --max-spend <n>   # unattended nightly
```
